VERDICT: BLOCKED

## Blockers

### 1. `docs/v4/implementation/beta12/cnpg18-direct-conformance.json` records a shape no committed command can emit

`scripts/beta12-conformance.ts` is the only conformance producer in the packet. It:

- validates `--target` against `"local" | "managed"` and exits 1 otherwise, so it can never write `"target": "remote"`;
- writes `profile` from a two-value ternary (`supabase-postgresql` | `local-postgresql-17`), so it can never write `"profile": "cnpg-postgresql-18-direct"`;
- never writes a `durationMs` field at all, yet the artifact carries `"durationMs": 126130.48`.

Meanwhile `docs/v4/implementation/beta12/backend-acceptance.md` asserts "The same `scripts/beta12-conformance.ts` command runs the identical packed BETA-12 scenario when standard PostgreSQL connection variables are supplied." The single remote PostgreSQL 18 PASS — one of the seven recorded verification results and a load-bearing element of acceptance criterion 5 — is therefore a hand-authored artifact with no reproducible producer.

Required repair: either extend the script to accept and emit the remote profile (so the artifact is regenerated by the recorded command), or remove the artifact and downgrade the remote claim to what was actually executed and can be re-executed. Evidence must be the script invocation and its written report at the committed path.

### 2. Two recorded verification commands cannot execute as recorded

`scripts/beta12-conformance.ts` requires `--report <path>`: `if ((target !== "local" && target !== "managed") || !reportPath) fail("use --target local|managed --report <path>")`, which exits 1 before any credential check, test spawn, or file write.

The manifest records:

- `bun run scripts/beta12-conformance.ts --target local against local PostgreSQL 17 ... PASS`
- `bun run scripts/beta12-conformance.ts --target managed without the selected Supabase credential writes managed-conformance.json as WITHHELD/MISSING_CREDENTIAL and exits 2 — PASS`

As written, both exit 1 with the usage error; the second writes no file and does not exit 2. No committed command writes `docs/v4/implementation/beta12/local-conformance.json` or `.../managed-conformance.json` — `tests/unit/beta12-release-contract.test.ts` passes `--report` to a temp path and deletes it. Both committed conformance artifacts consequently have no recorded producer, and the manifest's cited `23155.98 ms` local duration appears in no artifact the script writes.

Required repair: record the exact executed commands including `--report`, or give the script a target-derived default report path; then regenerate both artifacts from the recorded invocation.

### 3. Conformance `profile` and `postgresMajor` are operator-asserted, not measured

The script spawns `bun run test:postgres -- --scenario beta12` against ambient environment and ignores `--target` when doing so. `--target` only selects which credential names are required and which label is written; `postgresMajor` is read from `QUESTPIE_POSTGRES_MAJOR ?? "unreported"`. Running with local environment variables and `--target managed` would emit `profile: "supabase-postgresql"`, `status: "PASS"`, with nothing detecting the mismatch.

`backend-acceptance.md` rests its integrity claim on exactly this distinction ("it does not relabel CNPG as Supabase"), and acceptance criterion 5 depends on the labels being trustworthy. The tool structurally permits the mislabeling it promises not to do.

Required repair: derive `profile`/`postgresMajor` from the connected server (for example `server_version_num` and the resolved host) and fail when the observed endpoint contradicts the requested target, then regenerate the artifacts.

## Non-blocking observations

- `docs/v4/implementation/beta12/release-performance-report.md` says the `beta12-release-gate` scenario "validates all sixteen manifests through the repository performance schema." `tests/performance/beta12-release.test.ts` only `JSON.parse`s each manifest and asserts the distinct `budgetOwner` set equals `BETA-01..BETA-12`; it performs no schema validation and never asserts a count of sixteen. Schema validation plausibly lives in the `quality:release` performance gate, so criterion 9 is likely met elsewhere, but the attribution in the report is wrong and should be corrected.
- `tests/support/beta12-packed-questpie.ts` symlinks the repository's `node_modules/typescript` and `node_modules/@types` into the packed tracer application instead of installing the tarball's declared dependencies. The packed tracers are therefore not clean-consumer installs (the release dry-run's `bun install` path is). This is a real narrowing of criterion 4's "packed" claim and is not disclosed in `package-and-declaration-report.md`.
- `scripts/release.ts` dry-run creates `first`, `retry`, `consumer`, and `packed-application` at fixed paths inside the per-package loop with non-recursive `mkdirSync`. It works only because exactly one public package exists; a second publishable package would fail with `EEXIST` rather than a meaningful diagnostic.
- The `FAIL` branch of `scripts/beta12-conformance.ts` omits `profile`, so a failing report is shaped differently from the WITHHELD and PASS reports.
- `packages/questpie/package.json` adds `@types/bun` as a runtime `dependencies` entry. `typescript` is defensible (the vendored compiler needs it at runtime); a types-only package as a production dependency of the single public package is not obviously required and is not explained in the packaging report.
- Criterion 8 (`bun ci` plus `quality:release` before `npm publish --provenance`) is asserted in `release-provenance-report.md` but no workflow file appears in the diff; it is unverifiable from this packet and presumed pre-existing.
